message.content: The number of mitochondria in a cell varies widely depending on the cell type and its metabolic demands. In most mammalian cells, you’ll find roughly **50–200 mitochondria per cell**. However, specialized cells with high energy requirements—such as skeletal muscle fibers, cardiac myocytes, or neurons—can contain several thousand mitochondria each. Conversely, some cell types may have only a few dozen. Thus, while a “typical” cell has on the order of a few hundred mitochondria, the actual count can span from tens to thousands.
